summary: This program filters a list of farmers market products down to the organic summer ones, sorts them by price, and collects their names into a list. The only change from the earlier version is that the pipeline now runs on a parallel stream, which splits the work across several threads.

lines.text: Creates the collection the stream will read from. The book leaves the actual product data as comments, so running this file as printed produces an empty result list.
Calls the stream method and stores the finished list, keeping the pipeline itself out of main.

This is the one change that makes the pipeline parallel: instead of stream(), parallelStream() hands the elements to the common ForkJoinPool so that filtering and mapping happen on multiple threads at once.

Keeps only organic products whose season mentions summer. This lambda is safe in parallel because it only reads each product and stores nothing outside itself — a stateless lambda like this is the key requirement for parallel streams.
Sorts by price. In a parallel stream each chunk is sorted separately and the results are merged, which costs more than a sequential sort but still gives the same final order.
Replaces each product with its name, again using only the element itself so no thread can interfere with another.

Gathers the names. There is no thread safety concern here even in parallel: each thread collects into its own list and the collector combines them in order, so you never touch a shared mutable list yourself. Adding to an external ArrayList inside forEach is what would break.
